morphology: Continuous planar heteromorph shell: lower open coil feeds tangentially into long gently bowed shaft on the right, then a broad upper crook returning downward on the left, matchingFig2. Not three disconnected pieces or a spiral attached to a U-shaped handle.

Lower coil has a visible open central space and a small gap around its inner termination; preserve changing tube caliber and natural tangential growth. Do not create stacked rings, a tight normal ammonite disk or several unsupported complete turns.

Shaft remains long and only weakly curved; body-chamber caliber changes little. Upper hook is large and broadly rounded, with a visibly open gap separating its descending end from shaft. No closed loop.

Cross-sections are compressed and irregularly oval, not round pipes. Same fossil edge views constrain limited thickness. Slight local asymmetry from crushing is allowed, but centreline stays essentially planar.

Strong major transverse/oblique ribs and blunt nodules alternate with1–5 finer intercalary ribs in earlier shell. Shaft commonly1–2 finer ribs between major ones. Ribs strengthen around bend then become simpler toward end; do not use identical washer rings throughout.

The primary description distinguishes peridorsal, lateral and marginal tubercles on principal ribs. Simplify to low blunt swellings connected to ribs, not dense long spikes. Poorly preserved ventral details must stay subdued.
Final descending hook ends in a worn mineral-filled fossil face. No invented hollow black tunnel, thin lip, living soft parts or apertural teeth. Keep early coil end blunt and preserved-looking.

Historical plaster connector in coil: retain gross continuity required by documented specimen, with subdued smooth surface and no claim of original micro-ornament. Disclose in final metadata; do not copy all cracks, museum numbers or repaired seams as biology.
uncertainty: Selected specimen is nearly complete but partly repaired and compressed. This is an interpretation of its documented museum fossil form, not an unaltered specimen facsimile or living-shell restoration.

Published repair is identified by local whorl-height interval18–27mm, not an exact angular coordinate; do not assert an exact repair mask not supported by source. Use a subdued bridge rather than fabricated diagnostic detail.
Thumbnail edge photos do not permit precise thickness reconstruction;55mm working maximum may vary15–20%.
Stage is Lower Aptian, broad Cretaceous original retained; avoid old unsupported worldwide distributions or Barremian age assignments for this species.
palette: Matte muted grey-brown fossil; slight neutral material difference may distinguish conservatively inferred repair, not coloured biological pattern.
acceptance_focus: Front must show full lower coil, elongated shaft and large upper crook as one continuous growing structure, matchingFig2 without mirroring.
Side must show flattened fossil thickness, not a flat silhouette extrusion or a cylindrical hose.
Top/perspective must show open hook gap, separate early coil gap, varying ribs and filled termination.
No borrowing other Ancyloceratidae or B46085 missing coil; restoration limits explicit. Four standard views. Prep not scientific PASS.
